assertions.text: Multiple @TableTest methods are used, each addressing a distinct concern
assertions.evidence: Five separate methods: splitsByFulfillmentType, splitsByDeliveryAddress, shipsInStockItemsWithoutWaiting, minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses, keepsCompanionsTogether

assertions.text: Each @TableTest has only the rows needed to express its concern
assertions.evidence: splitsByFulfillmentType has 4 rows, splitsByDeliveryAddress has 4 rows, shipsInStockItemsWithoutWaiting has 4 rows, minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses has 4 rows, keepsCompanionsTogether has 3 rows

assertions.text: Fulfillment method splitting is represented as its own @TableTest
assertions.evidence: splitsByFulfillmentType method tests DELIVERY vs PICKUP: 'One delivery, one pickup | ... | 2 | [DELIVERY, PICKUP]'

assertions.text: Delivery address splitting is represented as its own @TableTest
assertions.evidence: splitsByDeliveryAddress method with scenarios like 'Two different addresses | [P1:1:DELIVERY:addr1, P2:1:DELIVERY:addr2] | 2'

assertions.text: Availability splitting is represented as its own @TableTest
assertions.evidence: shipsInStockItemsWithoutWaiting method with 'All in stock', 'All backordered', 'Pre-ordered separated from in-stock' scenarios

assertions.text: Warehouse allocation is represented as its own @TableTest
assertions.evidence: minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses method with scenarios like 'Two warehouses beats three' and Warehouses used? column

assertions.text: Companion product grouping is represented as its own @TableTest
assertions.evidence: keepsCompanionsTogether method with 'Companions co-located', 'Companions split when unavoidable' scenarios

assertions.text: Each @TableTest includes all output columns for its concern in the same table
assertions.evidence: splitsByFulfillmentType includes Shipment count? and Fulfillment types? in single table; minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses includes Shipment count? and Warehouses used? together

assertions.text: Warehouse allocation table uses scalar quantity columns
assertions.evidence: minimisesShipmentCountAcrossWarehouses uses 'Items | [P1:1, P2:1]' with scalar quantities, not detailed inventory maps

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: All tables begin with 'Scenario' as first column: 'Scenario | Items | ...'

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?'
assertions.evidence: Multiple columns end with '?': 'Shipment count?', 'Fulfillment types?', 'Immediate products?', 'Companion shipments?'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe the business situation
assertions.evidence: 'All delivery', 'One delivery, one pickup', 'Two warehouses beats three', 'Companions split when unavoidable'
'Shipment count?', 'Fulfillment types?', 'Warehouses used?', 'Companion shipments?' are all domain-oriented

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: Test bodies use only assertions: assertThat(...).hasSize(...), extracting(...), containsExactlyInAnyOrderElementsOf(...)
All methods follow pattern: @Description(...) @TableTest(...) void method(...) — @DisplayName is at class level

assertions.text: Test method has a clear, descriptive title
Multi-line @Description uses text block, not string concatenation
assertions.evidence: @Description('''...multi-line text...''') uses triple-quoted text block in shipsInStockItemsWithoutWaiting and other methods
